h1: Landscaping and garden care in Oak Bay
cardSummary: Character lots, estate gardens and Garry oak rock gardens, where deer and the Municipal Arborist permit shape most plans.
intro: Oak Bay is mostly established residential: large character lots in Uplands, family homes in South and North Oak Bay, condo stratas, and the village frontages along Oak Bay Avenue.

Deer are a real factor here. Oak Bay itself suggests deer-resistant plants, repaired fencing and barriers around accent plants and fruit trees, and protected trees need a Municipal Arborist permit before they are cut or damaged. See [landscape installation](/services/landscape-installation/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/?area=oak-bay).
propertyTypes: character and heritage homes on large lots
localRulesIntro: In Oak Bay the deciding step is the Municipal Arborist permit: no protected tree may be cut or damaged without one (or a development permit). Root-zone damage counts, which matters when renewing beds under mature oaks.

localNotes.title: Oak Bay tree permits
localNotes.text: In Oak Bay, no protected tree may be cut down or damaged unless authorized by a Municipal Arborist permit under the Tree Protection Bylaw or by a development permit. Check the bylaw for which trees are protected.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Deer pressure
conditions.body: Deer browse freely through Oak Bay gardens. New planting is chosen for deer resistance, and young or prized plants usually need a barrier until they are established.

conditions.title: Garry oak and rock in Uplands
conditions.body: Uplands and the streets around it have Garry oaks, rocky outcrops and mossy meadow edges. Those spots suit native, dry-summer planting better than thirsty lawn, and it helps to keep summer water away from oak trunks.

conditions.title: Salt air along the shore
conditions.body: Homes along Beach Drive near Willows Beach and McNeill Bay take salt spray and winter wind, which can scorch tender shrubs. Coastal-tolerant plants hold up better there.

topServices.why: Many older gardens are ready for renewal, and replanting with deer-resistant species is often the first request.
Estate and character gardens need detailed bed, hedge and leaf work that a quick mow-and-go visit does not cover.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Detailed bed care, hedge work and seasonal cleanups for established and estate gardens.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Garden renewals with deer-resistant planting, stone paths and drip irrigation.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Drip and spray systems adjusted to protect heritage stonework and mature beds.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Pruning and removals only after Oak Bay's tree permit rules have been checked.

jobNotes.title: Fall cleanup in a rock garden
jobNotes.body: Oak leaves were cleared from moss and rock pockets by hand rather than blown, and perennials were cut back while leaving seed heads standing over winter.

jobNotes.title: Spray moved off an oak’s root zone
jobNotes.body: A spray zone under a mature Garry oak was capped and the surrounding beds moved to drip, so the trunk and root zone stay dry through summer.

cta.heading: Get a free quote for your Oak Bay garden
cta.body: Let us know what deer have been eating and whether any large trees are near the work. Both shape the plan and the permit question.
